summary:
## Idea
A mutable minimum frontier. BinaryHeap retains push order among equal priorities; IndexedHeap maps non-negative integer keys to mutable priorities and restamps an updated key behind existing equal priorities.

## Complexity
Ordinary push/pop and indexed priority changes take O(log n) sift work; peek/count O(1). Array growth is additional. IndexedHeap stores positions through the greatest inserted key k, so its storage can be O(n+k), not O(n) for sparse keys. Rare insertion-stamp renumbering sorts n live stamps, O(n log n).

## Use when
Repeatedly select the least item, or decrease a keyed search frontier priority.

## Avoid when
A sorted one-shot scan suffices, or shared mutable access cannot be serialized.

## Pitfalls
A comparison must be consistent. The two equal-priority contracts differ; do not replace them with an unstable queue. Empty pop and invalid/duplicate indexed keys refuse.

## F# usage
Package: FS.GG.Algorithms; cited source API (resolve your actual package pin).
`FS.GG.Algorithms.Collections.BinaryHeap.create: ('T -> 'T -> int) -> BinaryHeap<'T>`

```fsharp
open FS.GG.Algorithms.Collections
let frontier = BinaryHeap.create compare
BinaryHeap.push 7 frontier
BinaryHeap.push 2 frontier
let first = BinaryHeap.pop frontier
```
